mainTopic: What is automatically included in a sale: a sand field with a pond, an olive press, and a bathhouse
overview: The amud opens by finishing a discussion about acquiring land. רב נחמן rules that taking possession of a sand field also acquires a pond sold with it. The גמרא explains that this adds something to שמואל's rule, because the two pieces of land have different uses. Next, a new משנה teaches what comes with the sale of a בית הבד (olive press): the fixed parts are included, the movable tools are not, and saying 'it and everything in it' includes them all. רבי אליעזר holds that the beam is always included. The גמרא defines each part and brings a ברייתא with a similar list, along with רבי אליעזר's reason: the press is named after the beam. A second משנה applies the same pattern to a bathhouse, and some things, like the water tanks, are never included. A ברייתא adds that the storage rooms are sold but the items in them are not, and it continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Taking the sand field acquires the pond
steps.stepSummary: רבה quotes רב נחמן: if someone bought a sand field and a pond together and did a קנין on the sand field, he acquires the pond too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said in the name of רב נחמן: If the buyer took possession of the sand field, he has also acquired the pond.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה reports a ruling of רב נחמן: one act of חזקה on the sand field acquires the pond that was sold along with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חזקה is a physical act of ownership that makes a purchase final. The new point is that this act on one piece of land counts for a second, different piece that was sold in the same deal.

keyTerms.meaning: took possession by doing an act of ownership (חזקה)
a pond or deep watery area

phrases.english: Rabba said that Rav Nachman said:
If he took possession of the sand field,
phrases.notes: The case is where the sand field and the pond were sold together in one deal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens this section with a ruling about acquiring two plots of land.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חזקה on the sand field also acquires the pond sold with it.

steps.title: Isn't this obvious from שמואל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that רב נחמן's ruling seems unnecessary, because שמואל already taught that one קנין acquires many fields sold together.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is obvious! שמואל already said: if he sold him ten fields, etc. (taking possession of one acquires them all).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב נחמן: why say something we already know from שמואל?
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל taught that when ten fields are sold together, a חזקה on one acquires all ten. If so, a sand field and a pond should obviously work the same way, so רב נחמן seems to add nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: it's obvious! (a challenge that a ruling teaches nothing new)
for indeed; introduces the source that makes it obvious
etc.; the rest of the quote is assumed

phrases.english: If he sold him ten fields, etc.!
phrases.notes: The full rule: ten fields in ten places, and taking possession of one acquires all of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether step 1 teaches anything new.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל's rule about ten fields already covers acquiring several plots with one חזקה, so the ruling is unnecessary.

steps.title: Different uses might have mattered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a sand field and a pond have different uses, so we might have thought they don't join together; רב נחמן teaches that they do.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: there (by שמואל) it works because it is all one kind of land, but here this one has its own use and that one has its own use. So he teaches us that it still works.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what new point רב נחמן is making beyond שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In שמואל's case all ten are fields, the same kind of land with the same use. A sand field and a pond are used in completely different ways, so we might have thought a חזקה on one can't reach the other. רב נחמן teaches that even different kinds of land sold together are acquired with one חזקה.

keyTerms.meaning: you might have said; introduces the mistaken thought being corrected
the block or body of land
so he teaches us (that the mistaken thought is wrong)

steps.whatToRemember: One חזקה acquires everything sold in the same deal, even pieces of land with different uses, like a sand field and a pond.

phrases.aramaic: הָתָם הוּא דְּסַדָּנָא דְאַרְעָא חַד הוּא,
phrases.english: there it works because the block of land is one,
phrases.notes: "There" means שמואל's ten fields, which are all the same kind of land.

phrases.english: this one has its own separate use,
and that one has its own separate use;

steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the ruling adds something new beyond the earlier source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Land with different uses (sand field vs. pond) might not be acquired together with one חזקה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even land with different uses, sold together, is acquired with one חזקה.

steps.title: What comes with an olive press sale
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that selling a בית הבד includes the ים, ממל and בתולות, but not the עבירים, גלגל and קורה, unless the seller says 'it and everything in it.'
steps.simpleTranslation: One who sells an olive press has sold the ים, the ממל and the בתולות, but not the עבירים, the גלגל and the קורה (beam). When he said 'it and everything in it,' all of them are sold.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins, listing which parts of an olive press go with it in a sale.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Parts that are fixed into the press count as part of the building and go with it automatically. Movable tools stay with the seller unless he uses the wider phrase 'it and everything in it.' The גמרא will soon explain what each strange name means.

keyTerms.meaning: an olive press, where oil is squeezed out
'it and everything in it'; a wider sale wording

phrases.english: One who sells an olive press

phrases.aramaic: מָכַר אֶת הַיָּם וְאֶת הַמֶּמֶל וְאֶת הַבְּתוּלוֹת,
phrases.english: has sold the yam, the memel and the betulot,
phrases.notes: These are names of parts of the press; the גמרא explains each one below.

phrases.english: but he has not sold the avirim
and the galgal and the beam.
And when he said to him:
"It and everything that is in it,"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: a new משנה about selling an olive press.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fixed parts of an olive press are included in its sale; movable tools are included only if he says 'it and everything in it.'

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: the beam is included
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר disagrees about the beam and holds it is sold with the olive press even without special wording.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: One who sells an olive press has sold the beam.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר argues on the first opinion of the משנה about the קורה (beam).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion counted the beam among the movable tools that are not included. רבי אליעזר holds the beam is included automatically, even though it is movable.

keyTerms.meaning: the heavy wooden beam that presses the olives
a תנא who disagrees here with the first opinion

phrases.english: One who sells an olive press

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the first opinion in step 4 about the beam.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The beam is included in the sale of an olive press.

steps.title: Defining the fixed parts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the three parts that are included: ים is the round basin, ממל is the crusher, and בתולות are the cedar posts that hold up the beam.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'ים' is the lentil-shaped basin. 'ממל': רבי אבא בר ממל said it is the crusher. 'בתולות': רבי יוחנן said they are cedar posts that hold up the beam.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts explaining the unusual words in the משנה, beginning with the parts that are included in the sale.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word gets a plain meaning. All three are parts that sit permanently in place, which fits why the משנה said they go with the press automatically.

keyTerms.meaning: literally 'lentil'; the round basin for the olives

phrases.notes: He means the round basin where olives are put, named for its round lentil shape.

phrases.english: with which they support the beam.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the included items listed in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ים = basin, ממל = crusher, בתולות = cedar posts holding the beam.

steps.title: Defining the movable tools
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the parts not included: עבירים are the pressing boards, גלגל is the weight-stone, and קורה is simply the beam.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'עבירים' are the pressers. 'גלגל' is the weight-stone. 'קורה' is just a beam.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes defining the words of the משנה, this time the tools that are not sold automatically.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are tools used for pressing that can be moved around, which is why the first opinion in the משנה did not include them without special wording.

keyTerms.meaning: pressing boards placed on the crushed olives
a round part of the press
a heavy stone used as a weight on the beam

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues step 6, now defining the items not included.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עבירים = pressers, גלגל = weight-stone, קורה = beam.

steps.title: The ברייתא's list of included parts
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists what comes with an olive press: the boards, the vats, the crushers and the lower millstone, but not the upper millstone.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: One who sells an olive press has sold the boards, the vats, the crushers and the lower millstone, but not the upper one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that gives its own list of what is included in selling an olive press.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same idea as the משנה shows up again: fixed parts go with the press. The lower millstone sits fixed in place so it is sold, while the upper millstone is movable and stays with the seller.

keyTerms.meaning: the Rabbis taught; introduces a ברייתא

phrases.english: One who sells an olive press

phrases.notes: The letters in square brackets are added in the corrected wording; it reads 'the boards.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא on the same topic as the משנה in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The boards, vats, crushers and lower millstone are included; the upper millstone is not.

steps.title: Saying 'everything in it' includes them all
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds, like the משנה, that if the seller says 'it and everything in it,' all the parts are sold.
steps.simpleTranslation: But when he said to him 'it and everything in it,' all of them are sold.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא repeats the משנה's rule that the wide wording 'it and everything in it' includes all the parts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With this wording, even the upper millstone and other movable parts go to the buyer. The next line will show that even this wording has a limit.

phrases.english: But when he said to him:
"It and everything that is in it,"

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבִזְמַן שֶׁאָמַר לוֹ הוּא וְכׇל מַה שֶּׁבְּתוֹכוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from step 8 with the wider wording.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With 'it and everything in it,' all the parts are sold.

steps.title: Items never included
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends by saying that in both cases, the עבירים, the sacks and the leather bags are not sold.
steps.simpleTranslation: Either way, he has not sold the עבירים, nor the sacks, nor the leather bags.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא sets a limit: some items are not sold even when the seller says 'it and everything in it.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Either way' means both with plain wording and with 'everything in it.' Sacks and leather bags are just carrying tools, not part of the press itself, so even the wide wording does not reach them. Notice that the ברייתא also lists the עבירים here, while the משנה seemed to include them with the wide wording.
steps.whatToRemember: Fixed parts go with an olive press automatically. Movable press tools go only with 'it and everything in it.' Carrying items like sacks and bags never go, according to the ברייתא.

phrases.notes: Whether he sold it plainly or said 'it and everything in it.'

phrases.english: he has not sold the avirim,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits step 9: even the wide wording does not include these items.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The עבירים, sacks and leather bags are never included in the sale of an olive press.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: The beam is sold with the olive press
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר rules that selling an olive press includes the beam, because the press is named after the beam.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: Someone who sells an olive press has also sold the beam, because the place is only called a 'בית הבד' because of the beam.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with רבי אליעזר's view, the same one quoted in the משנה (step 5), but now with his reason. He disagrees with the משנה's first opinion that the beam is not sold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה (step 4), the first opinion listed the beam (קורה) among the parts NOT included in the sale. The משנה gave רבי אליעזר's view without a reason, and the ברייתא now supplies it: בית הבד means 'house of the beam.' If the beam gives the whole place its name, it must be part of what was sold.

keyTerms.meaning: The heavy wooden beam used to press the olives
Another name for that pressing beam

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר holds that the beam is sold with the olive press, because the place gets its name from the beam. This closes the olive-press section.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the reasoning behind רבי אליעזר's view: if an item gives the property its name, it should go with the property. The first opinion in the משנה does not accept this for the beam.

phrases.aramaic: הַמּוֹכֵר בֵּית הַבַּד – מָכַר אֶת הַקּוֹרָה,
phrases.english: One who sells an olive press has sold the beam,
for it is not called a 'בית הבד'
phrases.notes: The beam is also called a בד, so בית הבד literally means 'house of the beam.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the ברייתא with רבי אליעזר's view from step 5, now giving his reason, against the משנה's first opinion in step 4 that the beam is not sold.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אליעזר, selling a בית הבד includes the קורה, since the press is named after it.

steps.title: New משנה: Selling a bathhouse does not include its movable items
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה rules that selling a bathhouse does not include the boards, basins or curtains.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Someone who sells a bathhouse has not sold the boards, the basins, or the curtains.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts a new case: selling a bathhouse (מרחץ). It lists items that do NOT come with the sale.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows the same pattern as the olive press. A plain sale includes the building, but not separate movable equipment used inside it. Boards, basins and curtains are separate objects, so the buyer does not get them automatically.

keyTerms.meaning: Curtains or cloths used in the bathhouse

phrases.english: nor the basins, nor the curtains.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה about a new kind of property, the bathhouse.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A plain sale of a bathhouse does not include the boards, basins or curtains.

steps.title: Saying 'it and everything in it' includes these items
steps.stepSummary: If the seller says he is selling the bathhouse and everything in it, the boards, basins and curtains are sold too.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he said to him, 'It and everything inside it,' all of these are sold.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds that the seller's wording can widen the sale. If he says 'everything in it,' the movable items are included.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The items from the last step are left out only because a plain sale does not mention them. Once the seller clearly says 'everything in it,' he has included them, so the buyer gets them.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It and everything that is in it,' a phrase that widens the sale

phrases.english: 'It and everything that is inside it,'
then all of them are sold.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּזְמַן שֶׁאָמַר לוֹ הִיא וְכָל מַה שֶּׁבְּתוֹכָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the case where the items from step 12 ARE included.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Saying 'it and everything in it' includes the boards, basins and curtains.

steps.title: Water tanks and wood storerooms are never included
steps.stepSummary: Whether or not the seller said 'everything in it,' the water tanks and wood storerooms are not sold.
steps.simpleTranslation: Either way, he has not sold the water tanks, and not the storerooms for wood.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists things that are not sold even with the wide wording 'everything in it.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Water tanks and wood storerooms are not really 'inside' the bathhouse. They are separate places that serve it. So even 'everything in it' does not cover them, and they need to be named clearly in the sale.

keyTerms.meaning: Storerooms for wood (fuel for heating the water)

steps.whatToRemember: There are three levels for a bathhouse sale: (1) the building is always sold, (2) movable items are sold only with 'everything in it,' (3) water tanks and wood storerooms are not sold either way.

phrases.english: Both in this case and in that case,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא מָכַר לֹא אֶת הַמְּגוּרוֹת שֶׁל מַיִם,
phrases.english: he has not sold the tanks of water,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets a limit: even the wide wording from step 13 does not include these.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Water tanks and wood storerooms are not sold, even when the seller says 'everything in it.'

steps.title: ברייתא: The storage rooms for the items are sold
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that a plain sale of a bathhouse includes the rooms where the boards, יקמין, basins and curtains are kept.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: Someone who sells a bathhouse has sold the room for the boards, the room for the יקמין, the room for the basins, and the room for the curtains.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that adds a new detail to the משנה. The storage rooms for the equipment are part of the sale.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only said the items themselves are not sold. The ברייתא makes clear that the rooms holding them are part of the building, so they do come with a plain sale. It also mentions a new item, יקמין.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for גמרא, the discussion on the משנה
'The Rabbis taught,' the opening of a ברייתא
The storage room for the boards
Curtains (the same idea as בלניות in the משנה)

phrases.english: has sold the room for the boards,
and the room for the יקמין,
and the room for the basins,
and the room for the curtains;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that fills in what the משנה did not mention: the storage rooms.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The storage rooms for bathhouse equipment are included in a plain sale of the bathhouse.

steps.title: But the items themselves are not sold
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא repeats that the boards, יקמין, basins and curtains themselves are not sold.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he has not sold the boards themselves, nor the יקמין themselves, nor the basins themselves, nor the curtains themselves.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא draws a clear line. The rooms are sold, but the objects inside them are not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This agrees with the משנה, which said the movable items are not sold. The word עצמן ('themselves') stresses the difference: the room belongs to the building, but the things stored in it stay with the seller.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the room with what is inside it. 'בית הנסרין' (the board room) is sold, but 'נסרין עצמן' (the boards themselves) are not.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits step 15: only the rooms are sold, not the objects in them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The bathhouse equipment itself is not included in a plain sale.

steps.title: ברייתא: 'It and everything in it' includes the items
steps.stepSummary: Like the משנה, the ברייתא says that if the seller says 'everything in it,' all the items are sold.
steps.simpleTranslation: And when he said to him, 'It and everything inside it,' all of them are sold.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא repeats the משנה's rule that the wide wording includes the movable items.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This matches step 13. Once the seller says 'everything in it,' the boards, יקמין, basins and curtains go to the buyer along with their rooms.

phrases.english: And when he said to him:

phrases.aramaic: ״הִיא וְכׇל מַה שֶּׁבְּתוֹכָהּ״ – הֲרֵי כּוּלָּן מְכוּרִין.
phrases.english: 'It and everything that is inside it,' then all of them are sold.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבִזְמַן שֶׁאָמַר לוֹ הִיא וְכָל מַה שֶּׁבְּתוֹכָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the case where the items from step 16 ARE sold, the same as the משנה in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With 'it and everything in it,' all the bathhouse equipment is sold.

steps.title: ברייתא: The water pools are not sold either way
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא begins to say that in both cases, the pools that supply water to the bathhouse are not sold. The sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: Either way, he has not sold him the pools that supply him with water, whether...
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא starts its 'either way' rule. Just like the משנה's water tanks, the pools that supply water are not sold. The sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This matches the משנה's rule in step 14 about water tanks. The pools that feed the bathhouse are separate from it, so even 'everything in it' does not cover them. The final word 'בין' ('whether') introduces cases that the ברייתא is about to list.

phrases.english: Both in this case and in that case,
he has not sold him the pools
that supply him with water, whether

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ לֹא מָכַר לוֹ אֶת הַבְּרֵיכוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets the limit on the wide wording from step 17, matching the משנה's step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The pools that supply water to the bathhouse are not sold, even with 'everything in it.'
